text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent weekly newspapers The Guardian and Mmegi (The Reporter) on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Letsibogo dam, part of the 1,200 million pula North-South Water Carrier project, is expected to be finished by April.

- Former Botswana Airways general manager Brian Pocock, for whom a warrant of arrest had been issued in Botswana, has been traced by the Financial Times and is living in Leicestershire, England. Pocock, 60, is sought by Botswana's Department of Corrupion and Economic Crime to answer allegations of corrupt practice arising from the purchase of BAe 146 aircraft by Air Botswana.

- Vice chancellor of the University of Botswana for the past 15 years, Dr Thomas Tlou, is likely to step down early this year, but plans to remain at the university as a teacher in the Department of History.

- A row has erupted between two rival factions of the Evangelical Lutheran Church. Members of the Lutheran Church of Southern Africa (ELCSA) at the weekend prevented members of the Lutheran Church in Botswana (ELCB), a breakaway faction seeking full atonomy in church matters formed 18 years ago, from entering church premises.
